classification.difficultyReason: Adds the two paths for exactly one pass and uses a complement for at least one pass.

content.prompt:
Becky has a maths test and then a science test.
She has an 80% chance of passing her maths test.
She has a 60% chance of passing her science test.
Assume the two test results are independent.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the probability she passes only one of the exams.

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}P(\text{maths pass, science fail})&=0.8\times0.4=0.32\\P(\text{maths fail, science pass})&=0.2\times0.6=0.12\\P(\text{only one pass})&=0.32+0.12\\P(\text{only one pass})&=0.44=44\%\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the probability she passes at least one of the exams.

answer.worked:
The complementary event is failing both tests.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{both fail})&=0.2\times0.4=0.08\\P(\text{at least one pass})&=1-P(\text{both fail})\\P(\text{at least one pass})&=1-0.08\\P(\text{at least one pass})&=0.92=92\%\end{aligned}$$
